context.transcript: [Test transcript written for this end-to-end test] Today I want to talk about why most automation projects fail. In our team we automated invoice processing last year. The first attempt failed because we automated a broken process: approvals bounced between three people and nobody owned exceptions. So step one was mapping the process on a whiteboard and removing two approval steps. Step two, we started with the most boring, high-volume case: standard supplier invoices, about 70 percent of our volume. Step three, every exception went to one named owner with a 24-hour response rule. After three months, the average processing time dropped from 6 days to 2 days. The lesson: fix the process first, automate the boring majority second, and give exceptions a human owner.
